display.title: Honoring the Chumash: Never on the Floor, Never Upside Down
display.summary_short: A Mitzvah Time lesson: never leave a Chumash on the floor or upside down, and the same goes for a Siddur and every holy sefer.
display.summary_long: A short Mitzvah Time lesson from the Tzivos Hashem radio show, part of a series on kibbud sifrei kodesh, honoring holy books. Uncle Yossi teaches two more rules. A Chumash may never be placed on the floor, which would be disrespectful; if you see one lying there, pick it up right away and put it in a safe and proper place. A Chumash should also never be left upside down, with the front cover on the bottom and the back cover on top. He suggests decorating the front cover so you always know which side is which, and reminds listeners that these rules apply to a Siddur, Nevi'im, Kesuvim and every holy sefer, so they will know the answers when he calls during Mitzvah Time.
display.lesson: Treat every holy sefer with respect: keep it off the floor and right side up.
